attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated in his own voice. He is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps all three firm assertions: costs too high, no path to profitability, and cost and ROI can't be measured. 'Too much' is evaluative and has no threshold. 'No path' looks partly forward, but it is stated as a present fact.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. A reproducible, fully costed measurement would refute 'can't measure', which is fair to the speaker. The Q1 2026 period and the unknown accounting basis are evaluator choices, and they block any decisive financial score.

evidence.note: Dated 2024 preprint that measures inference cost against accuracy on benchmarks. It comes before the target period and does not measure full task costs or commercial ROI, so it cannot refute the claim.
KPMG survey of finance leaders, fielded March 2026. It reports perceived ROI for AI broadly, not fully costed LLM task measurements, and says nothing about provider profitability.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no provider financials on a matching accounting basis. It also has no reproducible, fully costed task-ROI measurement from the period. e1 and e2 bear on the measurement assertion only indirectly and are out of scope, and nothing establishes or excludes a path to profitability. The evidence does not settle the bundled claim.
